pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as phase one with an explicit mobility-first framing that mapped directly onto his stated top goal: 'before we start focusing on getting you super strong... we got to make sure your body's moving properly. So we're going to give you the mobility routines, flexibility routines, get your body back into alignment.' Asked 'That making sense? Do you have any questions about that?' the prospect answered 'No.' He had arrived pre-sold on the modality itself — 'I found Kettleballs to be intriguing, and the videos that I saw posted to be inspiring' — and had bought kettlebells two days earlier, but he volunteered no reaction to the pillar as delivered.

Presented as the primal eating protocol with no calorie or macro counting. The prospect had already pre-empted it during discovery — 'I'm not coming to you necessarily asking for a meal plan... that's not the primary focus' — and during the pitch signalled he already knew it: 'I listened to one of his videos and he talked about his own diet.' Rep closed it with 'Even if you don't need it, it's always there' → 'Sure, of course.' Agreed without questions and without interest.

By far the most interrogated pillar and effectively the whole back half of the call. He asked how the form-video review works, then 'So is that required?', then 'would I actually be working with Trevor or would I be working with someone else?', then 'what's the procedure? What do I then receive and what do you then expect as a response?', then whether the videos are the free YouTube set, then whether programming is daily or weekly, then whether a three-week absence extends the six-month term. He was buying the delivery mechanism, not the training content, and every question was mechanical rather than sceptical.

anchors.raw: And are those what's currently on YouTube? Or it's another set of, because he's got a hundred or so videos on YouTube.
anchors.note: The most structurally important anchor in this batch. The funnel that produced this prospect is Trevor's free YouTube content — he found it two days before the call and had already begun copying the movements at his gym. When he asked whether the paid library is the same material, the rep conceded it might be: 'they might all be on YouTube if you want to go through like a hundred different videos.' A content-led funnel will generate this objection repeatedly and the playbook has no answer for it.

anchors.raw: It's more or less what I thought in terms of money, it's more or less what I thought it would be.
anchors.note: He arrived already anchored at or above $6,000 and confirmed it unprompted the moment the number landed. No discounting pressure existed on this call and none was applied — which makes the failure to collect payment a pure execution loss rather than a pricing one.

anchors.raw: I look at what the trainers at my gym are doing with clients. I also in some cases look at them and I say, there's really nothing that they could teach me... I've never been inspired to use them.
anchors.note: He disqualified the cheaper in-person substitute himself, on competence grounds, before the rep raised it. Combined with his rejection of Pilates and his refusal to use a trainer since the injury 30 years ago, every local alternative was already burned when the offer was made.

anchors.raw: I decided that I was, at that point, better off working out myself or working out with friends
anchors.note: Thirty years of self-programming is the real default option, and the rep did address it directly by naming the weekly-changing routine as the reason nothing progresses. Worth recording because it is the only alternative he had not already dismissed.

unmet_demand.want: A sample of the actual deliverable before paying — 'would you have an example of what your initial response would be in terms of setting out what you're asking for me to do over the course of a week or one workout... do you have any samples of that that perhaps you've created for other people?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep confirmed none exists: 'Well, we don't have like a generic one', and substituted a verbal description of a core mobility routine. A prospect buying a customised programming service asked to see one and there was nothing to show him.

unmet_demand.want: To see the onboarding questionnaire before committing — 'why don't you send me your onboarding questionnaire?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered that it is a post-purchase artifact ('that gets sent out when someone joins, but I can send it to you if you want to take a look at it') and immediately pivoted to the tier question. He had already read the form aloud on screen moments earlier, so the material plainly could be shared pre-sale; the process simply does not contemplate it.

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that coaching is genuinely one-to-one with Trevor personally, asked directly after being told there are over a thousand clients.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered by assertion only — 'We do have other coaches as well, but Trevor, it is one-on-one with Trevor' — with no detail on response times, review cadence or what the other coaches do. Nothing in the transcript establishes whether the claim holds at that client volume.

unmet_demand.want: Clarity on whether the six-month term pauses around his travel — he has six weeks of international travel booked from mid-June to end of July and asked whether an absence extends the term.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep committed verbally that it does — 'as long as you let us know, and it's no big deal to just extend the six months' — without reference to the written agreement the prospect had not yet seen. Whether the contract supports this is unestablished.
